answer.evidence: The top is a pyramid roof: rows 2-7 widen from 4 to 12 px, ending in a flat eave at row 7 (dark row, width 12). Row 8 is only slightly narrower (10) because the lantern body starts there, so the roof is a hat-shaped cap with a flat bottom, not an ellipse plate. The roof is read as a sloped roof plane above an eave line (evidence c). The lantern body (rows 8-17) and pole (rows 20-36, width 4) are front faces. The base (rows 39-47, widths 8-12-8) is a rounded ball that widens and narrows again, so it reads as an ellipse-like top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin standing lamp, so I judged it against prop-lamp-crook, the same kind. It has 9 visible tones per full tile and 0% near-flat coverage. Only 1% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark tone of the iron and not a black sticker line. By eye, the post has a lit and a shaded side, a stepped base, and a lantern with a glass glow and a cap. That is clearly richer than prop-lamp-crook, which is a nearly flat 1-2 tone pole with a 100% neutral outline. It is on par with prop-hedge (9 tones) but below the stall and well (17-20 tones), which are much bigger objects. The iron ramp has about 4 steps, a little under Beodeul's 5-6, but there are no flat fills and the piece would not look thinner or more sticker-like beside the reference lamp.

answer.evidence: The top end (rows 2-7) is a stepped trapezoid hat. Width goes 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 12 and then ends flat at row 7 on the narrower lantern (width 10). It is rounded only at its upper edge, with a flat bottom edge, so it is not an ellipse. Its colour is nearly uniform (L≈92 at x=8) with no receding top plane. The lantern body (rows 8-17) is a vertical face, and the 1-row plate at row 18 (width 12) is only a rim. The shaft (width 4, rows 20-36) has 2-row collars at rows 28-29 and 37-38 that are rims, not caps. The bulb foot (rows 39-47) widens and narrows like a dome, but it is at the bottom, not a cap on the top end. Every part is drawn as a front elevation with no horizontal top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin iron lamp, so I judged it by eye against prop-lamp-crook, the closest reference of the same kind. It has an ornate finial cap, a lantern with a lit glass core and frame, a pole with a collar, and a stepped base. The pole and base show about 4 lightness steps, a little fewer than the reference's 5-6. The measured facts support this: 9 visible tones in a full tile (the hedge reference also has 9), 0% near-flat coverage, and only 1% neutral dark edge pixels. That last figure means the outline is tinted to the iron and not a black sticker line. The crook lamp reference is a plain pole with a 100% neutral outline, so the candidate is at least as rich and its outline is better. It would sit acceptably next to the Beodeul props, though the iron ramp is a little shallow and the texture is modest, limited to a few highlight and shade dots.

answer.evidence: The top is a pointed pyramid roof whose width grows steadily from 2 to 12 over rows 0-7, then drops to 10 for the lantern. It is not an ellipse plate. Row 6 has a lighter edge pixel (L=147 at x=5) and row 7 is darker (L=63), which reads as a front-edge line plus eave shadow, so the roof counts as a sloped plane (evidence c). The lantern face (rows 8-17), the thin pole (width 4, rows 20-36) and the round base (rows 39-47) are all vertical or rounded forms with no horizontal top. The cap is a flat-bottomed hat that does not widen and narrow like an ellipse, so rounded_at_both_edges is false.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, tall lamp, so I compared it mainly with prop-lamp-crook, the closest reference of the same kind. The crook lamp is a nearly flat pole with a neutral near-black outline (100% neutral dark edges, about 3-4 steps). The candidate has more structure: a finial, a lantern with a lit glass panel, a collar, a shaded pole, and a stepped base. It shows about 9 visible tones per full tile, which matches prop-hedge and is well above the crook lamp. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Only 1% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark version of the metal, not a sticker line. It is still lighter than the stall and well, which reach 17-20 tones, but for a thin prop it holds up next to the references and does not look thinner or flatter than the crook lamp.
